question: outriggers going down on soft dirt, can we just set the floats on the ground and drop the jacks on top of em or do they gotta be pinned on
gold_answer: If outrigger floats are used, they must be attached to the outriggers. Stabilizer floats must likewise be attached to the stabilizers.

key_quote.text: When outrigger floats are used, they must be attached to the outriggers.

question: do we need to have the weights of the boom sections and counterweights on hand during assembly or is that just nice to have
gold_answer: It's required. The weight of each component must be readily available during assembly/disassembly.

key_quote.text: The weight of each of the components must be readily available.

question: Two questions: we're mixing boom inserts on an older crane and there's no manufacturer info on which combos are allowed, who signs off on that? And once it's put together does anyone have to look it over before we use it?
gold_answer: Component selection and configuration must follow manufacturer instructions/limits; if those are unavailable, a registered professional engineer familiar with that type of equipment must approve the selection and configuration in writing (or it must be an approved modification under 1926.1434). After assembly, the equipment must be inspected to confirm compliance (see 1926.1412(c)).

key_quote.text: a registered professional engineer familiar with the type of equipment involved must approve, in writing, the selection and configuration of components

question: During disassembly, what is required if we do not have enough information to accurately determine the center of gravity of a component we are lifting?
gold_answer: The center of gravity must be identified if that is needed for the method used to keep the load stable. If there isn't enough information to identify it accurately, you must use measures that prevent unintended dangerous movement from getting the center of gravity wrong (Appendix B gives an example).

key_quote.text: measures designed to prevent unintended dangerous movement resulting from an inaccurate identification of the center of gravity must be used

question: supplier knucklboom truck is bringing bundles of steel deck and wants to land them up on the joists for us, is that still delivry exemption or crane rules aply
gold_answer: The crane rules apply. The material-delivery exclusion does not cover structural steel members, and that explicitly includes steel decking, bundled or unbundled.

key_quote.text: structural steel member (for example, steel joists, beams, columns, steel decking (bundled or unbundled)

question: Tearing down a crawler. We already pulled the counterweight and now want to swing the upper around to lay the boom down and then walk it to the trailer. Anything the A/D director has to account for before we swing or travel?
gold_answer: Yes. The A/D director must address loss of backward stability before swinging the upperworks, before travel, and when attaching or removing components such as counterweight. They also have to address the hazard of unintended movement from counterweights that are not properly supported.

key_quote.text: Backward stability before swinging the upperworks, travel, and when attaching or removing equipment components.

question: Is a gin pole used to put up a cell tower covered by the crane standard? And what about a wrecker pulling a car out of the ditch next to our site?
gold_answer: Neither is covered. Subpart CC excludes gin poles used to erect communication towers, and it excludes automotive wreckers and tow trucks used to clear wrecks and haul vehicles.

question: Where the crane standard says an operator or crew member must do something, what obligation does that place on the employer?
gold_answer: The employer must set up work rules that ensure compliance with those provisions, communicate them effectively to the relevant people, and enforce them.

key_quote.text: the employer must establish, effectively communicate to the relevant persons, and enforce, work rules to ensure compliance with such provisions

question: when we lower the lattice stick to pull sections, the pendants keep hanging up on the cotter pins and keepers. is there an actual rule on that or is it just something to watch for
gold_answer: There's a rule. The A/D director must address snagging, and suspension ropes and pendants must not be allowed to catch on boom or jib connection pins or cotter pins, including keepers and locking pins.

key_quote.text: Suspension ropes and pendants must not be allowed to catch on the boom or jib connection pins or cotter pins (including keepers and locking pins).

question: drivin the crane empty past the service drop thats only 480 volts, how close can i get and do i still need a spoter for that
gold_answer: Under Table T, a line up to 0.75 kV (480 V is 0.48 kV) needs at least 4 ft of clearance while traveling with no load. If any part of the equipment will get closer than 20 ft to the line while traveling, a dedicated spotter in continuous contact with the driver/operator is still required.

key_quote.text: up to 0.75 | 4

question: We need to move the crane, no load, under a 345 kV line. Is the travel clearance the same 20 ft we'd use on Table A for operating at that voltage?
gold_answer: No. Table T requires 10 ft for over 50 to 345 kV while traveling with no load. Table A requires 20 ft for over 200 to 350 kV during operations.

key_quote.text: over 50 to 345 | 10

question: the laborer they gave me as a dedicated spotter for the lines, does he need any kind of training or can anybody just stand there and watch
gold_answer: Dedicated spotters must be trained so they can do the job effectively, including training on the applicable requirements of 1926.1408. The training has to be given in accordance with 1926.1430(g).

key_quote.text: must be trained to enable them to effectively perform their task, including training on the applicable requirements of this section

question: Our boom truck came from the factory with a proximity alarm. If we use it as our measure near the lines, can we set it up our own way or are there rules on how it gets used?
gold_answer: If a manufacturer-designed safety device, operational aid, or power-line contact prevention device is used to comply with 1926.1408, it must meet the manufacturer's procedures for use and conditions of use. The alarm also has to be set to give the operator enough warning to prevent encroachment.

key_quote.text: must meet the manufacturer's procedures for use and conditions of use

question: Erecting a tower crane with lines within 20 ft of where the jib goes. Two things: who has to be at the planning meeting, and are there any rules on the tag lines we use during erection?
gold_answer: The planning meeting must include the A/D director, the operator, the assembly/disassembly crew, and any other workers who will be in the assembly/disassembly area. In it they review where the lines are and the steps that will prevent encroachment. Any tag lines used must be nonconductive.

key_quote.text: If tag lines are used, they must be nonconductive.

question: if we go with a spotter as the extra measure while we're tearing down the crane by the lines what does the spotter need to have and where does he stand
gold_answer: During assembly/disassembly the dedicated spotter must be in continuous contact with the operator and have a visual aid for identifying the minimum clearance distance, such as a painted ground line, stanchions, or line-of-sight landmarks. The spotter must be positioned to effectively gauge clearance, use communication equipment where necessary, and give the operator timely information.

key_quote.text: Be equipped with a visual aid to assist in identifying the minimum clearance distance.

question: For a job breaching Table A, does the procedure have to be written down, and who's actually in charge of running it?
gold_answer: The procedures must be documented and immediately available on-site. The utility owner/operator (or RPE) and all employers involved must identify one person to direct implementation, and that person must have authority to stop work at any time to ensure safety.

key_quote.text: must have the authority to stop work at any time to ensure safety.

question: power co killed and grounded the line last week for another contractor. super says its still dead so we're good to swing over there today. right?
gold_answer: No. All power lines must be treated as energized unless the utility owner/operator confirms that the line has been and continues to be deenergized and visibly grounded at the worksite. A superintendent's word or last week's outage doesn't count.

key_quote.text: has been and continues to be deenergized and visibly grounded at the worksite

question: rough terrain crane bouncing across a rutted site no load under lines, boom bobs up and down. what does the reg say about that besides keeping the table T distance
gold_answer: The boom/mast and its support system must be lowered enough to meet the travel requirements. The employer must also consider how speed and terrain affect equipment movement, including boom/mast movement, so that those effects don't cause a breach of the Table T clearances.

key_quote.text: The effects of speed and terrain on equipment movement (including movement of the boom/mast) are considered

question: working inside table A on the crawler next week who puts the cover up on the lines does the rigging gotta be anything special and can the extra guys hang around to watch
gold_answer: The utility owner/operator must install insulating line hose or cover-up unless none is available for the voltage involved. Rigging must be nonconductive if it may be within the Table A distance. Only personnel essential to the operation are allowed in the area of the crane and load.

key_quote.text: Insulating line hose or cover-up must be installed by the utility owner/operator except where such devices are unavailable for the line voltages involved.

question: guy at the shop wants to slather the hoist line in that thick black tar dope so it lasts longer, any problem with that come inspection time
gold_answer: Rope lubricants of a type that hinder inspection must not be used. A heavy coating that hides the rope's condition from the inspector is not allowed.

key_quote.text: Rope lubricants that are of the type that hinder inspection must not be used.

question: befor we cut the wire rope to length do we need to put seizings on it, one side or both sides, and how many
gold_answer: Yes. Before cutting a wire rope, seizings must be placed on each side of the cut point. The length and number of seizings must follow the wire rope manufacturer's instructions.

key_quote.text: Prior to cutting a wire rope, seizings must be placed on each side of the point to be cut.

question: We have two lattice boom crawlers doing general hoisting. One was built in 2005 and its anti-two-block system only sounds a warning. The other was built in 2013 and has the same warning-only system. Is that OK on both machines?
gold_answer: On the 2005 crane (built after Feb 28, 1992), a device that warns the operator in time to prevent two-blocking at all points where it could occur is acceptable. A lattice boom crane built after November 8, 2011 must have a device that automatically prevents damage and load failure, so a warning-only system is not enough on the 2013 crane.

key_quote.text: Lattice boom cranes and derricks manufactured after November 8, 2011 must be equipped with a device which automatically prevents damage and load failure

variant: general hoisting, not the dragline/clamshell exception

question: drum rotation indicator quit on our 2015 machine and i cant see the drum from the seat what do i do til its fixed and how long do we have
gold_answer: Equipment built after Nov 8, 2011 with a hoist drum not visible from the operator's station needs a hoist drum rotation indicator. Until it's fixed, mark the drum to show its rotation, and install mirrors or remote video cameras and displays if the operator needs them to see the mark. As a Category II aid it must be repaired within 30 calendar days. If parts were ordered within 7 days and haven't arrived in time, the repair is due within 7 days of receiving them.

key_quote.text: Mark the drum to indicate the rotation of the drum.

question: The foot pedal brake lock on our crane is busted. Is that lock actually required? And can we work around it with some other measure until it's fixed, like the workarounds allowed for operational aids?
gold_answer: Yes. Equipment with foot pedal brakes must have locks, and the lock is a listed safety device. Operations must not begin unless it works properly. The equipment must be taken out of service until it is fixed, and alternative measures are not permitted.

key_quote.text: Alternative measures are not permitted to be used.

question: On the shift check I counted 7 random broken wires in one lay on the main hoist line. The rope maker has a written removal criterion for this exact rope that allows more broken wires than OSHA's number. Can we keep running it?
gold_answer: This is a Category II deficiency, so the rope can't be used until the employer complies with the manufacturer's established removal criterion (or a different one the manufacturer approved in writing for that specific rope), replaces the rope, or, if the damage is localized, cuts out the damaged section (no splicing, at least two wraps left on the drum at the lowest position). So you may keep running it if the manufacturer's criterion for this exact rope applies and the rope is within it.

key_quote.text: The employer complies with the wire rope manufacturer's established criterion for removal from service or a different criterion that the wire rope manufacturer has approved in writing for that specific wire rope

expert_review.why: Whether a manufacturer's more lenient criterion allows continued use turns on how the criterion is read and documented.

question: found a whole strand popped on the whip line, is that rope junk or can we chop it, and do we gotta lock out the whole rig or just that drum
gold_answer: A broken strand is a Category III deficiency. The rope must be replaced, or if the damage is localized it can be cut in two and the undamaged part used (no splicing, at least two wraps left on the drum at the lowest position). Until then, either the whole equipment or the hoist with that rope must be tagged out.

key_quote.text: either the equipment (as a whole) or the hoist with that wire rope must be tagged-out

question: our boom truck is rated 5000 lbs built 2008, does it legaly have to have a load moment indicater or load weighing thing
gold_answer: No. The requirement for a load weighing device, load moment indicator or limiter applies only to equipment (other than derricks and articulating cranes) built after March 29, 2003 with a rated capacity over 6,000 pounds. A 5,000 lb rated machine is below that threshold.

key_quote.text: manufactured after March 29, 2003 with a rated capacity over 6,000 pounds must have at least one of the following

question: knuckle boom with a winch, built 2016, A2B is out. we can two-block it just by extending the boom without touching the winch. whats the fix til parts come
gold_answer: Do both: mark the cable where the operator can easily see it, at a point that gives enough time to stop the hoist, and use a spotter when extending the boom. A2B is a Category I aid and must be repaired within 7 calendar days, or, if the employer documents that parts were ordered within 7 calendar days of the failure, within 7 calendar days of receiving them.

key_quote.text: clearly mark the cable (so that it can easily be seen by the operator) at a point that will give the operator sufficient time to stop the hoist to prevent two-blocking, and use a spotter when extending the boom

variant: built after Dec 31, 1999, equipped with load hoist

question: Beyond what the shift inspection covers, what must the annual comprehensive wire rope inspection cover, and which areas of the rope need particular attention?
gold_answer: A qualified person must do a complete, thorough inspection of the surface of the entire length of the ropes for the Category I-III deficiency types. Particular attention goes to the critical review items, sections normally hidden during shift and monthly inspections, rope subject to reverse bends, and rope passing over sheaves.

key_quote.text: covering the surface of the entire length of the wire ropes

question: how far down can i boom down or drop the hook before im too low on the drum, like how many wraps gotta stay on
gold_answer: You can't lower the load or the boom below the point where fewer than two full wraps of rope stay on its drum. At least two full wraps have to remain on each drum.

key_quote.text: Neither the load nor the boom must be lowered below the point where less than two full wraps of rope remain on their respective drums.

question: am i allowed to be on my cell phone while im running the crane what if im using it to talk to the signal guy
gold_answer: No. While actually operating, you can't do anything that diverts your attention, including using a cell phone, except for signal communications. If a phone is used for signals, the electronic-signal rules in §1926.1421 also apply: the device must be tested on site before operations begin, signals must go through a dedicated channel (subject to that section's exceptions), and your reception must be hands-free.

key_quote.text: such as the use of cellular phones (other than when used for signal communications)

question: we run sidebooms on the pipline, do the operaters need the crane certifcation and if not do they need any traning at all
gold_answer: Sideboom crane operators are exempt from the §1926.1427 certification and evaluation requirements. They still have to be trained, though: the employer must train each exempted operator on the safe operation of the equipment they will use, under §1926.1430(c).

key_quote.text: The employer must train each operator covered under the exception of § 1926.1427(a)(2) on the safe operation of the equipment the operator will be using.

question: Two things on our truck crane: can we hang extra counterweight past what the manufacturer lists to get more capacity, and can we run it with part of the counterweight left off for a light job?
gold_answer: No to both. You can't exceed the manufacturer's maximum counterweight or ballast, and you can't operate without the counterweight or ballast in place as the manufacturer specifies. (Tower cranes are covered separately, under §1926.1435(b)(8).)

key_quote.text: The maximum counterweight or ballast specified by the manufacturer for the equipment must not be exceeded.

question: We've got an old 1979 friction crawler with a live boom. Next job is picking pipe inside a refinery and nobody will be under the load. Can we run it with the free-fall boom there?
gold_answer: No. A live (free-fall) boom is prohibited whenever lifting takes place in a refinery or tank farm, even if no one is in the fall zone. Being built before October 31, 1984 only allows a live boom where none of the prohibited circumstances apply.

key_quote.text: Lifting operations are taking place in a refinery or tank farm.

question: For a fall restraint system used on a crane, how strong must the anchorage point on the equipment be, and may body belts be used rather than full harnesses?
gold_answer: A fall restraint system must be anchored to a part of the equipment that can withstand twice the maximum load an employee could put on it under reasonably anticipated conditions of use. Under §1926.1423(d), either body belts or body harnesses may be used in a fall restraint system.

key_quote.text: capable of withstanding twice the maximum load that an employee may impose on it during reasonably anticipated conditions of use

question: two different subs got cranes on site and their booms can reach into each others area, no GC really running things. whose job is it to sort that out
gold_answer: When any part of one crane is within the working radius of another, the controlling entity must set up a system to coordinate operations. If there is no controlling entity, the employers operating the equipment must set up that system (or the single employer, if only one runs all the equipment).

key_quote.text: If there is no controlling entity, the employer (if there is only one employer operating the multiple pieces of equipment), or employers, must institute such a system.

question: My trainee is getting good. Can he run the man basket pick, can he be one of the cranes on a tandem lift, and can he do a christmas tree multi-lift rigging pick if I sign off on him?
gold_answer: An operator-in-training can't hoist personnel or operate in multiple-equipment lifts, and a sign-off doesn't change that. Multiple-lift rigging is also prohibited unless the operator's trainer determines that the trainee's skills are sufficient for this high-skill work.

key_quote.text: In multiple-lift rigging operations, except where the operator's trainer determines that the operator-in-training's skills are sufficient for this high-skill work.

question: new guy ran cranes in the army, has his military crane qual. he's working for us now, a private contractor. does that qual count as his cert?
gold_answer: No. A U.S. military qualification only meets §1926.1427 for employees of the U.S. military, meaning federal employees of the Department of Defense or Armed Forces, and not private contractors. It also isn't portable: it only counts while the operator works for the employer that issued it.

key_quote.text: An employee of the U.S. military is a Federal employee of the Department of Defense or Armed Forces and does not include employees of private contractors.

question: If none of the accredited testing organizations offer a certification exam for the specific type of crane our operator runs, how does he meet the certification requirement, and what has to be on his certificate?
gold_answer: He's treated as compliant if he's certified for the type of equipment most similar to his machine that does have a certification exam. His certificate must state the type of equipment he's certified for.

key_quote.text: certified for the type that is most similar to that equipment and for which a certification examination is available

expert_review.why: Deciding which certified type is 'most similar' to a given machine is a judgment call the text doesn't define.

question: lowering a guy down a 6 ft drill shaft on a bosun chair can we send two guys at once to save time and does somebody gotta be at the top of the hole
gold_answer: No. With a boatswain's chair, only one person may be hoisted at a time. A signal person must be stationed at the shaft opening, and the employee must wear a full body harness attached independently of the crane/derrick.

key_quote.text: No more than one person must be hoisted at a time.

question: rigging the man basket off a crane with rotation resistant hoist rope. what safety factor do the slings need, do the eyes need thimbles, and can we use that bridle to pick materials the rest of the week?
gold_answer: When rotation resistant rope is used, the slings must support at least 10 times the maximum intended load (other rigging hardware and hooks need at least 5 times). Eyes in wire rope slings must have thimbles. The platform bridles and rigging may be used only for hoisting personnel and their tools and materials, never for anything else.

key_quote.text: Where rotation resistant rope is used, the slings must be capable of supporting without failure at least ten times the maximum intended load.

question: Our basket has its own controls in it. Can the operator step out of the cab while the guy in the basket runs it himself?
gold_answer: No. While a platform with controls is occupied, the equipment operator must be at a set of equipment controls that include the boom and swing functions, on site and in view of the equipment. The occupant using the platform controls must be a qualified person for using them, and the platform operating manual must be in the platform or on the equipment.

key_quote.text: The equipment operator must be at a set of equipment controls that include boom and swing functions of the equipment, and must be on site and in view of the equipment.

question: 2 hammerheads goin up on the same site, how close can they be? can one jib swing over the other
gold_answer: When more than one fixed-jib (hammerhead) tower crane is on a jobsite, they must be placed so no crane can contact the structure of another crane. Cranes are allowed to pass over one another.

key_quote.text: the cranes must be located such that no crane can come in contact with the structure of another crane.

question: LMI on the tower crane is fried. what do we have to do to keep picking and how long till it has to be fixed
gold_answer: The load moment limiting device is a Category I aid. As a temporary measure, use a radius indicating device (or measure the radius if the crane has none) and determine the load weight from an industry-recognized source or calculation, giving that to the operator before the lift. The repair is due within 7 calendar days, or within 7 calendar days of receiving parts if the parts were documented as ordered within 7 days.

key_quote.text: A radius indicating device must be used (if the tower crane is not equipped with a radius indicating device, the radius must be measured to ensure the load is within the rated capacity of the crane).

expert_review.why: Manufacturer may specify more protective alternative measures that must be followed.

question: What rules apply when a worker is handling rope on the winch head of a derrick?
gold_answer: Ropes may not be handled on a winch head unless the operator knows about it. While the winch head is in use, the operator must be within reach of the power unit control lever.

key_quote.text: While a winch head is being used, the operator must be within reach of the power unit control lever.

question: old guy derrick no boom angle indicator on it is that a problem
gold_answer: A boom angle indicator isn't required on a derrick. Without a working one, though, you need one of two things: caution and stop marks on the boom hoist cable matching the maximum and minimum allowable boom angles, visible to the operator or to a spotter in direct communication with the operator; or an electronic or other device that warns the operator in time or automatically stops the boom from going past those angles.

key_quote.text: The stop marks must correspond to maximum and minimum allowable boom angles.

question: For a crane permanently mounted on a barge and built for marine use, what wind speed do the load charts have to account for, and what is the minimum freeboard needed for stability at rated capacity plus 25 percent?
gold_answer: The load charts must account for a wind speed of at least 40 mph. Per Table M2, at rated capacity plus 25% the equipment must be stable in a 60 mph wind with at least 1 ft of freeboard (2 ft at rated capacity and at high boom with no load).

key_quote.text: Rated capacity plus 25% | 60 | 1

question: on the barge theres no room to rope off the swing radius of the crane like we do on land. how are we supposed to mark it off
gold_answer: On a barge the employer can do either of two things: put up and maintain control lines, warning lines, railings or similar barriers at the hazard-area boundaries; or mark the hazard areas clearly with warning signs (e.g., "Danger—Swing/Crush Zone") plus high-visibility markings on the equipment. With the signs-and-markings option, every employee must be trained on what the markings mean.

question: For our little crane rated under 2000 lbs, does the operator need certified, and what inspection schedule do we follow — the usual shift/monthly/annual?
gold_answer: No operator certification is required for equipment rated 2,000 lbs or less, but the employer must train each operator on safe operation of that type of equipment before they run it. Equipment inspections follow the manufacturer's procedures rather than the general equipment inspection schedule. However, the post-assembly inspection in 1926.1412(c) and the wire rope requirements in 1926.1413-1414, including 1413's shift, monthly and annual wire rope inspections, still apply.

key_quote.text: The employer must ensure that equipment is inspected in accordance with manufacturer procedures.

expert_review.why: Answer relies on 1926.1427 and 1926.1412 shift/monthly/annual not being listed in 1441(a); only 1412(c) post-assembly applies.

question: Under 1910.179, what stopping performance must the bridge bumpers on an overhead crane meet, and how much energy must they be able to absorb?
gold_answer: The bridge bumpers must stop the crane, not counting the lifted load, at an average deceleration of no more than 3 ft/s/s when it is traveling in either direction at 20% of rated load speed. They must also absorb enough energy to stop the crane at a speed of at least 40% of rated load speed, and they must be mounted so there is no direct shear on the bolts.

key_quote.text: at an average rate of deceleration not to exceed 3 ft/s/s when traveling in either direction at 20 percent of the rated load speed

question: We're adding a second trolley on the same bridge girders in our shop. Do both trolleys need bumpers where they could run into each other, and what's the stopping spec for trolley bumpers?
gold_answer: Yes. When more than one trolley runs on the same bridge, each trolley must have bumpers or an equivalent device on the ends that face each other. Trolley bumpers must stop the trolley, not counting the lifted load, at an average deceleration of no more than 4.7 ft/s/s when it is traveling in either direction at one-third of rated load speed.

key_quote.text: at an average rate of deceleration not to exceed 4.7 ft/s/s when traveling in either direction at one-third of the rated load speed

question: hoist rope sizng on a bridge crane, how do i know the rope is strong enuf for the rated load with multiple parts of line
gold_answer: Follow the crane manufacturer's recommendation. The rated load divided by the number of parts of rope must not be more than 20% of the rope's nominal breaking strength. Replacement rope must be the same size, grade and construction as the original unless a wire rope manufacturer recommends otherwise for the actual working conditions.

key_quote.text: The rated load divided by the number of parts of rope shall not exceed 20 percent of the nominal breaking strength of the rope.

question: loco crane on the spur next to the main yard track can i swing the boom out over toward the other track what do i need first
gold_answer: Do not swing a locomotive crane into a position where railway cars on the adjacent track could hit it. First confirm that cars are not being moved on that track and that proper flag protection is in place.

key_quote.text: until it has been ascertained that cars are not being moved on the adjacent track and proper flag protection has been established

question: crawler's running low, can I top it off from a jerry can without shutting her down? and what kind of extinguisher am I supposed to have on the rig
gold_answer: No. Machines must not be refueled with the engine running. Small portable containers must be approved safety cans with an automatic closing cap and a flame arrester. A carbon dioxide, dry chemical or equivalent fire extinguisher must be kept in the cab or near the crane.

key_quote.text: an approved safety type can equipped with an automatic closing cap and flame arrester

question: Two-part question for our plant truck crane: when are we actually required to put the outriggers out, and if we crib under the floats with wood blocks, what does the blocking have to meet?
gold_answer: Outriggers must be used when the load at that radius is more than the manufacturer's rated load without outriggers. Floats must be securely attached to the outriggers. Wood blocks under the outriggers must be strong enough not to crush, free from defects, and wide and long enough that they will not shift or topple under load.

key_quote.text: Outriggers shall be used when the load to be handled at that particular radius exceeds the rated load without outriggers as given by the manufacturer for that crane.

question: is there a rule on how short a wire rope sling can be made
gold_answer: Yes, and it depends on the type. Cable laid, 6x19 and 6x37 slings need at least 10 times the component rope diameter of clear rope between splices, sleeves or end fittings. Braided slings need 40 times the component rope diameter between loops or end fittings. Cable laid grommets, strand laid grommets and endless slings need a circumferential length of at least 96 times their body diameter.

key_quote.text: Braided slings shall have a minimum clear length of wire rope 40 times the component rope diameter between the loops or end fittings.

question: I spliced an eye in a 3/4 inch nylon rope sling and want to cut the tails off flush so they don't snag. Is that allowed? If not, how long do the tails have to be, and what can I do if they get in the way?
gold_answer: No. Strand end tails must not be trimmed flush next to the full tucks. For rope under 1 inch, the tails must stick out at least six rope diameters past the last full tuck (about 4.5 inches for 3/4 inch rope); for rope 1 inch and larger, at least 6 inches. If the tails interfere with using the sling, taper them and splice them into the rope body with at least two more tucks.

key_quote.text: For fiber rope under one inch in diameter, the tail shall project at least six rope diameters beyond the last full tuck.

question: What handle damage takes a metal mesh sling out of service? Give me the limits for the female handle slot, the eye width, and wear around the handle eye.
gold_answer: Remove the sling from service if any of these is true: the female handle is distorted so the slot depth has increased by more than 10%; either handle is distorted so the eye width has decreased by more than 10%; the original metal cross-section anywhere around the handle eye is reduced by 15%; or either handle is bent out of its plane.

key_quote.text: A 15 percent reduction of the original cross sectional area of metal at any point around the handle eye.

question: them web straps near the dryer get pretty warm, how hot can nylon or poly straps go before we cant use em, is polypro any different
gold_answer: Polyester and nylon synthetic web slings must not be used above 180°F. Polypropylene web slings must not be used above 200°F.

key_quote.text: Synthetic web slings of polyester and nylon shall not be used at temperatures in excess of 180 °F. Polypropylene web slings shall not be used at temperatures in excess of 200 °F.

expert_review.why: In the field, "poly" can mean polyester or polypropylene, and the temperature limits differ (180°F vs 200°F).
